#### Assess and initial QC sequencing data with NanoPlot
Install [Nanoplot](https://github.com/wdecoster/NanoPlot) in conda environment
conda creates a 'bubble' to run nanoplot within 
```{bash, eval = FALSE}

#!/bin/bash

############# run_nanoplot.sbatch  ###################
# Run nanoplot on unaligned ONT bams to generate quality assessment plots

# load required modules 
module load miniconda3

# activate conda environemnt 
conda activate nanoplot

# read array key and set variables
SAMPLE=$(sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p" $ARRAY_KEY)
BAM="${INDIR}/${SAMPLE}.bam"
SAMPLEDIR="${OUTDIR}/${SAMPLE}"

if [ ! -d $SAMPLEDIR ]; then mkdir $SAMPLEDIR; fi

# run NanoPlot
NanoPlot -t ${CPUS} --ubam ${BAM} --plots dot -o ${SAMPLEDIR}

echo "Done with ${SAMPLE}"

# END SCRIPT



```





Run Nanoplot
```{bash, eval = FALSE}
# copy code to a script in your github repository called run_nanoplot.sbatch

#!/bin/bash

# wrapper-run_nanoplot.sh 
# This script starts an array job to run nanoplot on unaligned bam files
# Last updated 03/11/2026 by MI Clark

# define high level variables
date=$(date +%m%d%Y)
echo running on $date 
jobname=nanoplot

#define dirs:
indir="/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Raw" # name of directory with the alignments to run qualimap on
outdir="/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Raw/nanoplot" # name of directory where qualimap reports can live
logfilesdir="/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Logs/nanoplot" #name of directory to create and then write log files to

#check if directories have been created; if not, make 
if [ ! -d $logfilesdir ]; then mkdir $logfilesdir; fi
if [ ! -d $outdir ]; then mkdir $outdir; fi

# make alignment key
# this file should be a list of sample names
# e.g., 
# ind1	ind2    ind3    ind4
array_key="/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorp/Scripts/nanoplot_key.txt"

SAMPLE_LIST=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
    SAMPLE_LIST+=("$line")
done < <(find "${indir}" -maxdepth 1 -name "*.bam" | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.bam$//' | sort)
printf '%s\n' "${SAMPLE_LIST[@]}" > $array_key

echo "Found ${#SAMPLE_LIST[@]} samples"

# define slurm job details
cpus=1 #number of CPUs to request/use per dataset
ram_per_cpu=25G #amount of RAM to request/use per CPU CHANGE
array_no=$(cat $array_key | wc -l) # number of array jobs to run 

# define executable and reference genome 
executable=/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Scripts/run_nanoplot.sbatch #script to run 

#---------------------------------------------------------

#submit job to cluster
sbatch --job-name=$jobname \
	--array=1-$array_no%6 \
	--export=ARRAY_KEY=$array_key,CPUS=$cpus,INDIR=$indir,OUTDIR=$outdir,LOGFILESDIR=$logfilesdir \
	--cpus-per-task=$cpus \
	--mem-per-cpu=$ram_per_cpu \
	--output=$logfilesdir/${jobname}_${date}_%A-%a.out \
	--error=$logfilesdir/${jobname}_${date}_%A-%a.err \
	--time=4:00:00 \
    --partition=lab-mpinsky \
    --qos=pi-mpinsky \
    --account=pi-mpinsky \
	$executable
		
echo submitted $array_no jobs to run nanoplot on bams in $indir

echo ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo My executable is $executable		



```

WRAPPER: wrapper-filter_align.sh
```{bash, eval = FALSE}

#!/bin/bash

# wrapper-filter_align.sh
# This script starts an array job to filter and align ONT reads in unaligned bam files
# Last updated 03/11/2026 by MI Clark

# define high level variables
date=$(date +%m%d%Y)
echo running on $date 
jobname=filter_align

#define dirs:
homedir="/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph" # home directory for project
#scratchdir="/hb/scratch/miclark/kelpMorphMIC" # name of directory to use for temporary files during filtering and alignment
### 

indir="${homedir}/Data/Raw" # name of directory with unaligned bam files
logfilesdir="${homedir}/Logs/filter_align" #name of directory to create and then write log files to
outdir="${homedir}/Data/Alignments" # name of directory where alignments can live 

#check if directories have been created; if not, make 
if [ ! -d $logfilesdir ]; then mkdir $logfilesdir; fi
if [ ! -d $outdir ]; then mkdir $outdir; fi

# make array key
# this file should be a list of sample names
# e.g., 
# ind1	ind2    ind3    ind4
array_key="${homedir}/Scripts/filter_align_key.txt"

# find list of files with .bam extention in the input directory, remove the extention and file path, and write a list of sample names to the array key
SAMPLE_LIST=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
    SAMPLE_LIST+=("$line")
done < <(find "${indir}" -maxdepth 1 -name "*.bam" | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.bam$//' | sort)
printf '%s\n' "${SAMPLE_LIST[@]}" > $array_key

echo "Found ${#SAMPLE_LIST[@]} samples"

# define slurm job details
cpus=8 #number of CPUs to request/use per dataset
totalmem=120G #amount of RAM to request/use per CPU CHANGE
array_no=$(cat $array_key | wc -l) # number of array jobs to run 

# define executable and reference genome 
executable=${homedir}/Scripts/filter_align.sbatch #script to run 
reference=${homedir}/Data/Reference/MpyrReferenceGenome1.fasta # reference genome to align to

#---------------------------------------------------------

#submit job to cluster
sbatch --job-name=$jobname \
	--array=1-$array_no%2 \
	--export=ARRAY_KEY=$array_key,CPUS=$cpus,INDIR=$indir,OUTDIR=$outdir,LOGFILESDIR=$logfilesdir,SCRATCHDIR=$scratchdir,REFERENCE=$reference \
	--cpus-per-task=$cpus \
	--mem=$totalmem \
	--output=$logfilesdir/${jobname}_${date}_%A-%a.out \
	--error=$logfilesdir/${jobname}_${date}_%A-%a.err \
	--time=24:00:00 \
    --partition=lab-mpinsky \
    --qos=pi-mpinsky \
    --account=pi-mpinsky \
	$executable
		
echo submitted $array_no jobs to filter and align bams in $indir

echo ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo My executable is $executable

```

EXECUTABLE: filter_align.sbatch
```{bash, eval = FALSE}
#!/bin/bash

############# filter_align.sbatch  ###################
# Filter and align ONT bams with chopper and minimap2
# Last updated 03/12/2026 by MI Clark

# load required modules 
module load miniconda3

# activate conda environemnt 
conda activate chopper

# read array key and set variables
SAMPLE=$(sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p" $ARRAY_KEY)
BAM="${INDIR}/${SAMPLE}.bam"

# this following command converts input bams to fastq, filters then with chopper using a 
# length cut-off of >1000bp and mean quality scores >Q10, and then aligns the filtered reads to the reference genome with minimap2
samtools fastq ${BAM} | chopper -l 1000 -q 10 | \
  minimap2 -ax map-ont --MD -t ${CPUS} ${REFERENCE} - | \
  samtools sort -o ${OUTDIR}/${SAMPLE}_aligned.bam

# index bam file
samtools index -@ ${CPUS} ${OUTDIR}/${SAMPLE}_aligned.bam

echo "Done with ${SAMPLE}"

# END SCRIPT
```

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
#open conda

BAM="${INDIR}/${SAMPLE}.bam"

# this following command converts input bams to fastq, filters then with chopper using a 
# length cut-off of >1000bp and mean quality scores >Q10, filters again with filtlong, and then aligns the filtered reads to the reference genome with minimap2
samtools fastq ${BAM} | chopper -l 1000 -q 10 | \ filtlong --min_length 1000 
--keep_percent 90 --target_bases 500000000 input.fastq.gz | gzip > output.fastq.gz | \
  minimap2 -ax map-ont --MD -t ${CPUS} ${REFERENCE} - | \
  samtools sort -o ${OUTDIR}/${SAMPLE}_aligned.bam

# index bam file
samtools index -@ ${CPUS} ${OUTDIR}/${SAMPLE}_aligned.bam

echo "Done with ${SAMPLE}"

# END SCRIPT
```

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
#!/bin/bash

# wrapper-run_qualimap.sh 
# This script starts an array job to run qualimap on aligned bam files
# Last updated 03/12/2026 by MI Clark

# define high level variables
date=$(date +%m%d%Y)
echo running on $date 
jobname=qualimap

#define dirs:
### CHANGE WHEN RUNNING IN NEW DIRECTORY ### 
homedir="/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph" # home directory for project
### 

indir="${homedir}/Data/Alignments" # name of directory with the alignments to run qualimap on

if [ ! -d $logfilesdir ]; then mkdir $logfilesdir; fi
if [ ! -d $outdir ]; then mkdir $outdir; fi

# make key

SAMPLE_LIST=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
    SAMPLE_LIST+=("$line")
done < <(find "${indir}" -maxdepth 1 -name "*.bam" | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.bam$//' | sort)
printf '%s\n' "${SAMPLE_LIST[@]}" > $array_key

echo "Found ${#SAMPLE_LIST[@]} samples"

# define slurm job details
cpus=1 #number of CPUs to request/use per dataset
ram_per_cpu=50G #amount of RAM to request/use per CPU CHANGE

# define executable and reference genome
```

EXECUTABLE: run_qualimap.sbatch
```{bash, eval = FALSE}

#!/bin/bash

# run_qualimap.sbatch
# This script uses qualimap to generate alignment statistics for a given sample.
# Last updated 03/02/2026 by MI Clark

#--------------- EXECUTABLE ---------------

# Input: Reference genome path, forward and reverse reads from wrapper-align_to_genome.sh 
#
# Output: ${SAMPLE_NAME}.bam file, forward and reverse reads aligned to reference genome and trimmed

# activate conda environment
module load miniconda3
conda activate qualimap

SAMPLE=$(sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p" $ARRAY_KEY)
BAM="${INDIR}/${SAMPLE}.bam"
SAMPLEDIR="${OUTDIR}/${SAMPLE}"
# run qualimap 

# java-mem-size should be ~75% of requested RAM
qualimap bamqc \
    -bam "${BAM}" \
    -outdir "${SAMPLEDIR}" \
    -outformat HTML \
    --java-mem-size=37G \
    -nt "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
    --paint-chromosome-limits

echo "Done with ${SAMPLE}"

## END SCRIPT
 
```



#### Call SVs with sniffles2

#### Call SVs with sniffles2

We will call SVs with sniffles2. Sniffles2 is not good at calling SVs in repetitive regions of the genome, and will sometimes split large variants into smaller false positives in repetitive regions.
To avoid this, we will provide Sniffles2 with a tandem-repeat mask for the reference genome. A tandem repeat is a sequence of DNA that is repeated multiple times in a row. 
We will use Tandem Repeats Finder (TRF) to identify tandem repeats in the reference genome, and then use the output to create a mask for Sniffles2.

```{bash, eval = FALSE}

#SLURm script


#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=tandemrepeats
#SBATCH --output /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Logs/tandemrepeats-%j.out
#SBATCH --error /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Logs/tandemrepeats-%j.err
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --time=168:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=250G 
#SBATCH --partition=lab-mpinsky
#SBATCH --qos=pi-mpinsky
#SBATCH --account=pi-mpinsky

# TRF is already installed as a module on Elkhorn. 

# It is loaded as follows: 
module load trf/4.09.1

# run TRF
# recommended parameters: 
 trf /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/MpyrReferenceGenome1.fasta 2 7 7 80 10 50 500 -d -f -m

# convert to bed file # A basic awk parser mapping TRF .dat fields to 0-based BED format
awk -v OFS='\t' '$1 == "Sequence:" {fa = $2; next} ; NF == 15 {print fa, $1, $2}' /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/tandem_repeats/MpyrReferenceGenome1.fasta.2.7.7.80.10.50.500.dat > /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/repeat_mask.bed

# load bed tools 
module load bedtools
# sort bed file 
bedtools sort -i /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/repeat_mask.bed > /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/final_repeat_mask.bed


echo "Done wth TRF"

#opening up an interactive node to work on if needed:
salloc --time=24:00:00 --mem=100Gb --ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task=5 --partition=lab-mpinsky \
        --qos=pi-mpinsky \
        --account=pi-mpinsky


```


```{bash, eval = FALSE}

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=sniffles
#SBATCH --output /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Logs/sniffles-%j.out
#SBATCH --error /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Logs/sniffles-%j.err
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=32
#SBATCH --time=168:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=200G 
#SBATCH --partition=lab-mpinsky
#SBATCH --qos=pi-mpinsky
#SBATCH --account=pi-mpinsky

# load conda module
module load miniconda3
# activate conda environment
conda activate sniffles

module load parallel/20200122

module list

# CHANGE ME! 
REFERENCE=/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/MpyrReferenceGenome1.fasta
OUTDIR=/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/SVs
INDIR=/home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Alignments
SAMPLES=(SWCinteg001 SWCinteg002 SWCpyr006 SWCpyr010 SWCpyr051 SWCpyr053)
# 

TOTAL_CPUS=${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}
PARALLEL_JOBS=6
CPUS_PER_SAMPLE=$(( TOTAL_CPUS / PARALLEL_JOBS )) # CPUs each sniffles instance gets

mkdir -p ${OUTDIR}/snf

# per-sample SNF calling in parallel
echo "Starting per-sample SNF calling..."

parallel --jobs ${PARALLEL_JOBS} --halt now,fail=1 \
    sniffles \
        --input ${INDIR}/{}_aligned.bam \
        --snf ${OUTDIR}/snf/{}.snf \
        --reference ${REFERENCE} \
        --threads ${CPUS_PER_SAMPLE} \
        --sample-id {} \
        --tandem-repeats /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/final_repeat_mask.bed \
    ::: "${SAMPLES[@]}"

# --halt now,fail=1 kills all jobs  if a  sample fails so joint genotyping never runs on incomplete data

# joint genotyping
echo "Starting joint genotyping..."

sniffles \
    --input ${OUTDIR}/snf/*.snf \
    --vcf ${OUTDIR}/kelpMorph_SVs.vcf.gz \
    --reference ${REFERENCE} \
    --tandem-repeats /home/cmdowlin/kelpMorph/Data/Reference/final_repeat_mask.bed \
    --threads ${TOTAL_CPUS}
echo "Done."

```
